main_text.p: ophrastus, cum iis quæ discipulus ejus Phædro, cognomento Magnus, de Hermaphroditi anima refert, & patebit Monarchiæ Chymicæ principibus, unde existat, &quo modo paretur Hermaphroditi flos ille Sapphiricus, qui est admirandū majoris mundi mysterium, quippe cujus drachma (inquit) post sui projectionem super tria drachmarum millia liquati auri, in Mille aris drachmas immissa, id universum in aurum transmutat purissimū. Hæc PhædroRodocheus: cujus processus nos quosdam latet.
His addere non immerito possumus, quæ experientissimus vir & Naturæ indagator profundissimus Joannes Isaacus Flander (ab hoc enim cæteri ætate posteriores omnes, velut ab altero Hermete, didicerunt)

page.notes: The first line of the text is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Some words in the italic passage are hard to read in the scan ("purissimū" read as printed, "Rodocheus" as printed). The catchword "C" and "cerunt)" are at the foot of the block; the "C" is treated as a catchword-like signature mark and "cerunt)" completes the final line.
